Clare Culture & Creativity Team
The Heritage Officer as part of the Clare Culture & Creativity 
Team has been funded by the Clare County Council’s Creative 
Ireland fund to undertake the 11th Reading the Local Landscape 
Course. This very successful course will be run in partnership 
with the Limerick Clare Education and Training Board and the 
Irish Community Archive Network (iCAN*) - a National Museum 
of Ireland initiative which supports local communities to share 
their local history and heritage through a step-by-step training 
and mentorship programme. 
Shanakyle Bog Creative Biodiversity and 
Archaeology Project
Also with funding from the Clare County Council’s Creative 
Ireland fund, the Heritage Officer and Biodiversity Officer are 
working together on the Shanakyle Bog Creative Biodiversity and 
Archaeology Project. Working with the Shanakyle Bog Restoration 
Group, the landowners, Limerick College of Art, Cathy Moore 
and Clare Archaeological & Historical Societies. Cathy Moore is a 
leading expert in Irish peatland/wetland archaeology and partner 
to the Irish Peatland Archaeology Across Time Project (IPeAAT) 
in UCC. Cathy will introduce the students at Limerick College of 
Art and members from the local community to peatland/wetland 
archaeology with specific focus on the archaeology of the 
Shanakyle Bog area. Research will include cartographic sources, 
the archives of the National Museum of Ireland and local reports 
and accounts. 
Students and community members will be encouraged to 
consider how bogs were viewed and used by people in the past 
and their role today in the modern landscape as reconfigured 
peatland habitat through rewetting efforts. The students from 
the Limerick School of Art and Design and community members 
will attend the lectures and workshop given by both Cathy Moore 
and Barry O’Loughlin (on the rewetting project and the ecology 
of the bog) and from this will produce a response and a display 
which will showcase their work in art form for an exhibition.

National Barrier Mitigation Programme: Scheme 2
Inland Fisheries Ireland’s National Barrier Mitigation Programme 
(NBMP) is working to reconnect Ireland’s rivers by mitigating 
and removing man-made barriers that impact fish migration, 
water quality, biodiversity, and hydromorphology. The scheme 
supports Ireland’s targets under the EU Biodiversity Strategy 
2030, the Water Framework Directive (WFD), and national plans 
such as the Water Action Plan 2024 and Ireland’s 4th National 
Biodiversity Action Plan. Further details of the Fund 2 Scheme is 
at the link https://www.fisheriesireland.ie/funding-schemes 
Council Biodiversity Project: Craggaunowen 
Biodiversity Conservation Plan 
As part of Clare County Council’s Biodiversity Officer 
Work Programme, an ecological survey was completed at 
Craggunaowen and a Biodiversity Conservation Plan was 
prepared to identify, evaluate and conserve the existing habitats 
of the site and identify new opportunities to enhance the 
habitats, flora and fauna for biodiversity (e.g. bats, birds, rare 
plants). Clare County Council’s Biodiversity Officer engaged 
Wetland Surveys Ireland to undertake the surveys. The site is 
dominated by habitats comprising broadleaved woodland with 
cutover bog and grassland. The bat surveys identified eight out 
of the nine regularly occurring bat species in Ireland within the 
Craggaunowen site. The site also supports the rare plant, Yellow 
Birds-nest (Hypopitys monotropa) within an area of woodland. 
Several biodiversity actions such as installing bat roost boxes, 
implementing wildflower meadows to benefit pollinators, sand 
martin nest colonies, barn owl boxes, biodiversity interpretation, 
citizen science, etc were drafted to enhance the site for flora 
and fauna and to serve as an educational resource for the local 
community. 
 
Craggaunowen supports broadleaved woodland including oak-ash-
hazel woodland and wet willow-alder-ash woodland.

DEVELOPMENT
The Town and Village Renewal Scheme (TVRS) 2025 is a national 
government programme supporting the regeneration of rural 
towns and villages. Its aim is to revitalise town centres, reduce 
vacancy and dereliction, and improve the social, economic and 
cultural vitality of rural communities. 
Funding under the 2025 scheme supports:
•	
Reuse of vacant or derelict buildings
•	
Community, cultural and recreational facilities
•	
Public realm and town centre enhancement projects
•	
Project planning and design through the Project Development 
Measure
In 2025, €824,480 was allocated to County Clare to support three 
projects focused on community infrastructure, youth services 
and cultural spaces, strengthening town centres and improving 
quality of life for local communities. The approved projects were:
•	
Mountshannon Community Council received €500,000 to 
refurbish and extend the community hall, creating a modern 
cultural, arts and market space to increase activity and 
footfall in the village.
•	
Fishbowl Youth - Scariff was awarded €274,480 to redevelop 
a derelict former co-op building into a permanent youth 
centre serving the East Clare area.
•	
Miltown Malbay Creative Centre received €50,000 under 
the Project Development Measure to support design and 
planning work for the expansion of the Design Bank creative 
hub, including the reuse of a former bank building.
Local Enhancement Programme (LEP) 2026
Clare Local Community Development Committee (LCDC), as 
a statutory committee of Clare County Council, is pleased to 
announce the Local Enhancement Programme (LEP) is open for 
online applications from Friday, 23rd January 2026. The Local 
Enhancement Programme is funded by the Department of 
Rural & Community Development and the Gaeltacht (DRCDG), 
the funding available to Clare LCDC for the 2026 programme is 
€181,061.31 
The Local Enhancement Programme 2026 will help support groups 
with necessary repairs and small capital works/improvements 
to their facilities, energy efficiency type projects, purchase of

scheme, primarily that funding may now only be assigned to 
capital projects, there is no provision for current, day to day

grants of €1,000 or less. 
The LEP grant is administered by Clare Local Community

funding is targeted locally towards addressing disadvantage to 
the areas that need it most. The fund is strategically aligned with 
the Clare Local Economic and Community Plan 2024-2030.

LOCAL AUTHORITY INTEGRATION 
TEAM 
 
The Local Authority Integration Teams (LAITs) have been set up 
in all local authorities. Their purpose is to help coordinate the 
different kinds of support available for people who are applying 
for international protection, refugees, and others in similar 
situations. 
The goal of LAITs is to help IP applicants and refugees become 
independent, settle into their new communities, and participate 
in Irish life. They do this by connecting people to important 
services that can help them integrate into the community. 
Who do LAITs support? 
LAITs provide support for: 
•	
Applicants for International Protection (IP) 
•	
People who have been granted refugee status or other forms 
of protection, such as subsidiary protection or permission to 
remain 
•	
Refugees who have been resettled in Ireland through a 
government programme 
•	
Beneficiaries of Temporary Protection (BOTPs)  
How is the support provided? 
LAITs operate under the principle of 'Integration from Day One'. 
This means that LAITs provide integration support to people who 
need it as soon as they arrive in Ireland. 
What services do LAITs provide? 
The work of LAITs isn’t meant to replace existing services. Instead, 
LAITs help connect people with the existing services that are most 
suitable for their needs. This includes things like: 
•	
Being a direct contact for new arrivals, helping them with any 
problems they might have when dealing with public services 
•	
Connecting new arrivals with services like legal help, 
childcare and healthcare 
•	
Connecting new arrivals with services that improve their 
ability to live independently, like job training, English classes, 
education, and apprenticeships 
•	
Guiding new arrivals through the process of applying for 
financial support, medical help, child benefits, and other 
services they might need 
•	
Holding meetings in local areas and using community 
development principles to help those who attend 
•	
Supporting people if they face racism or other unfair 
treatment, helping them report it to the right authorities 
•	
Helping vulnerable new arrivals get in touch with non-
governmental organisations (NGOs) and other services if 
they need extra help 
How do I contact my Local Authority Integration Team? 
You can contact LAIT's by email on integration@clarecoco.ie 
The LAIT Team continues to deliver information and signposting

TOWN CENTRE FIRST
Draft Kilrush Town Centre First Plan 
Kilrush Town Team, supported by Clare County Council’s Town 
Centre First Department, West Clare elected members, and 
Council staff, has prepared a Draft Town Centre First (TCF) 
Plan. The draft Plan aims to provide the town with a path to 
regeneration. It sets out a shared vision for a thriving, vibrant, 
and sustainable Kilrush, informed by the voices of residents, 
community groups, and businesses. The plan is built around six 
themes: Inclusion, Climate & Biodiversity, Vibrancy, Heritage, 
Culture, and Wellbeing. 
Public consultation on this plan took place on 4 December in 
Kilrush Town Hall, with a positive flow of engagement. The 
online platform Have Your Say is now closed, and all feedback is 
currently being compiled to progress the plan toward completion 
in early February.
 
Lisdoonvarna Project Development Measure.
Clare County Council, in partnership with Grafton Architects, 
the Lisdoonvarna Town Team, and a range of local stakeholders, 
continues to advance the development of a detailed Public Realm 
Design for Lisdoonvarna Town Square.
All required site surveys have now been completed. The first 
public consultation for the design stage of this project—building 
on insights gathered during the Tapping the Well town‑wide 
engagement initiative—is scheduled to take place in February 
2026.
The project team is currently preparing detailed design proposals, 
with a Part VIII Planning Application expected to be submitted 
by summer 2026. Once delivered, the project will provide a 
high‑quality, architecturally designed public realm space at the 
heart of Lisdoonvarna, enhancing the town centre for residents, 
visitors, and local businesses.
At this stage, capital funding for the construction phase has not 
yet been secured. Clare County Council and project partners will 
continue to explore suitable funding opportunities as the project 
progresses toward planning.

Co-Creating Works
Ennis MD crews continued to work on the Co-Creating project 
in January. This project involves the tightening of junctions and 
the installation of raised pedestrian crossings throughout key 
locations in the town to improve accessibility and pedestrian 
safety. To date, in excess of 30 junctions in Ennis have been 
upgraded under this scheme. The latest improvements were 
carried out include at Carmody St, College Road, Kilrush Road and 
McNamara Park.
O’Connell St - Partial Pedestrianisation
In January Ennis MD announced a Section 38 proposal to introduce 
permanent partial pedestrianisation of O’Connell Street. This 
proposal comes in response to significant engagement with 
the public and businesses within Ennis Town Centre. Results of 
surveys carried out over the Christmas period show a significant 
appetite for the pedestrianisation of O’Connell St with almost 
90% of the public and 80% of businesses calling for some form of

is on the critical path for the Ennis Town Bus Service Project. We 
expect that the construction of the bus stops will commence in 
February 2026. It is envisaged that the Ennis Town Bus Service 
will commence during Summer 2026.

This unit operates within the Housing Delivery, Infrastructure 
Provision and Land Activation Directorate and the key objective 
across all the elements of the unit is to bring together our 
resources with a strong ambition for delivery of increased 
activity on lands and activation of vacant and derelict properties 
throughout the County.
Working collaboratively across the other units in the Directorate 
with pooled resources and knowledge, it is intended to increase 
levels of activity and engagement to activate more properties for 
delivery of housing, both public and private.
Work towards ending dereliction and vacancy is a priority in the 
National Housing Plan 2025, with the re-use and regeneration 
of vacant and derelict properties in cities, towns and villages 
providing much needed housing and transforming and revitalising 
communities, as summarised hereunder.
 
DERELICT SITES
A significant effort to transform the many derelict properties 
across the County is underway with 313 derelict properties 
being dealt with under the Derelict Sites Act 1990 as of the 
21st January 2026. The team maintains very high levels of 
activity and engagement with owners and their legal/technical 
representatives. This initial engagement is key to resolution of 
the issues of dereliction and to gain an understanding of the 
various reasons why the properties are in a derelict state. Where 
derelict properties are sold by the owner, the Derelict Sites Team 
engages promptly with the new owners to brief them on their 
responsibilities under the Derelict Sites Act, 1990. 
To bolster the momentum, the Council is advising property 
owners on accessing the vacant property refurbishment grant. 
The Team is also seeing a consistent number of planning 
applications for property refurbishment/extensions, and it is 
clear from driving around the county the level of work ongoing 
on individual properties. The Derelict Sites Team believe that by 
working in partnership with owners and financial institutions, 
there are real opportunities for the positive revitalisation and re-
development of many properties.

Feasibility Study on the Mountain Biking in Slieve 
Bearnaghs
The feasibility study on the mountain biking in Slieve Bearnaghs 
awarded to Killaloe Municipal District under the Outdoor 
Recreation Improvement Scheme (ORIS) is now complete. 
The study proposes a network of 46 km of trails, combining 
purpose built singletrack with upgraded forest roads to cater for 
beginners, families, and experienced riders alike. The trails are 
intended to be free or low cost, offering a safe and enjoyable 
way for people of all ages to get active in nature.
The study also examined the landscape, environmental 
considerations, and the potential economic benefits. Findings 
suggest that mountain biking could bring significant tourism 
and local business gains, while helping to build a cycling culture 
in the community. 
Funding is required to progress this project with some sections 
of the proposed trail network dependent on future wind 
farm developments. The study reports strong potential for a 
sustainable and high quality project with benefits for residents 
and visitors.
